summary: 2 Esdras 15 (63 verses) continues the story of faithfulness. Starting with '“Behold, speak in the ears of my people the words of prophecy which I will put in your mouth,” says the Lord.', it moves through themes of faithfulness, wisdom and calls readers toward hope.
whyItMatters: This chapter matters because it shows faithfulness lived out in second temple period. For a first-time reader, it answers: who is God in this moment, what does he ask, and how do people respond.

keyVerses.text: “Behold, speak in the ears of my people the words of prophecy which I will put in your mouth,” says the Lord.
then these will be troubled, and keep silence through their power, and will turn and flee.
They will carry your children away captive, and will plunder your wealth, and mar the glory of your face.”

questions.question: What is happening in 2 Esdras 15?
questions.answer: In 63 verses, this chapter 2 esdras 15 (63 verses) continues the story of faithfulness. starting with '“behold, speak in the ears of my people the words of prophecy which i will put in your mouth,” says the lord.', it moves through themes of faithfulness, wisdom and calls readers toward hope. The setting is second temple period, written to jewish community. Look for who speaks, who listens, and what changes by the end.

questions.question: Who wrote 2 Esdras and why 15 matters in the bigger story?
questions.answer: Traditionally anonymous / tradition, addressed to jewish community around intertestamental. This chapter fits the book's purpose as jewish literature — its themes of faithfulness, wisdom build on what came before.

questions.question: What does 'faith' mean in this chapter?
questions.answer: Trust, loyalty to God. In this chapter, it appears in context of faithfulness. For a first-time reader: think of it as trust, loyalty to god, not just religious jargon.

questions.question: What does this chapter teach about God or people?
questions.answer: Through faithfulness and wisdom, it shows God's character (faithful, just, merciful) and human tendency (need, failure, hope). Notice how verses move from problem to provision.

questions.question: Verse 8 is long — what is it saying in plain English?
questions.answer: The verse says: '“I will hold my peace no more concerning their wickedness which they profanely commit, neither will I tolerate them in these things, which they wickedly practice. Behold, the innoc...' In plain terms: it is making a key point about faithfulness. Break it into two halves — what is described, and what is promised or commanded.

questions.question: How could this chapter apply today without forcing modern ideas onto it?
questions.answer: Ask: what was original audience supposed to do with this? Then ask: what similar situation exists today? For example, if chapter warns about idols, today that might be money or status; if it celebrates deliverance, where do people need deliverance today?
